attack_mechanism: When the instruction decoder selects R4 as `reg_src` or `reg_dest`, the execution unit presents its value to the ALU operand network. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add_inc` is an operand, result, or status-producing intermediate reached while the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`. An internal probe of `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add_inc` during a chosen MOV, logical, add, or shift operation reveals R4 directly or as a known reversible function. The operative RTL path is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.op_src_inv -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add_inc`. The observation bypasses direct protection of R4; even a one-bit flag leaks a predicate that can be accumulated over chosen operations.

The observation bypasses direct protection of R4; even a one-bit flag leaks a predicate that can be accumulated over chosen operations.

An instruction that uses R4 as a source operand, store datum, or address base transfers its contents from the register file into the memory address/data backbone. `openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.eu_pmem_addr` carries the resulting address, data word, or bus-selected derivative when the transfer is guarded in the RTL by `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.src_reg_src_sel`. Probing `openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.eu_pmem_addr` during that transaction exposes R4 directly for a move/store or reveals a deterministic address/data function of R4. The operative RTL path is `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.op_src_inv -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.alu_0.alu_add -> openMSP430.mem_backbone_0.eu_pmem_addr`. The observation discloses all or part of the confidential R4 value and repeated chosen instructions can resolve otherwise masked bits.
